newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fukutoku Bank to write off Y17.6 bln bad loans.
newsitem.headline: Fukutoku Bank to write off Y17.6 bln bad loans.

text.p: Japan's Fukutoku Bank Ltd said it plans to write off problem loans worth 17.6 billion yen in the year ending on March 31.

The regional bank operating in the Kansai area of western Japan said in a statement it expects its problem loans to ordinary clients to fall 35.7 percent year-on-year to a total of 53.6 billion yen as of March 31. This would be equivalent to 4.1 percent of the bank's total lending, it said.
Fukutoku said it has taken necessary measures to cope with the problem loans partly by raising loan loss reserves.
Problem loans to the bank's non-bank financial affiliates, meanwhile, are forecast total 49 billion yen as of March 31, down 4.1 percent from a year earlier, it said.
It said it would not have to shoulder any additional burden to support its troubled financial affiliates.

The planned bad loan write-offs this fiscal year would trim the bank's capital adequacy ratio to around 4.0 percent at the end of this month, but the ratio may recover to 4.3 percent by September, the bank said.

Under its current restructuring plan, the bank said it plans to cut the number of workers to 1,500 and branches to 100 by March 1999. At the end of this month, the bank said it will have a total 1,900 workers and 117 branches.
